question:
Samia set off on her bicycle to visit her friend, traveling at an average speed of \(17\) kilometers per hour. When she had gone half the distance to her friend’s house, a tire went flat, and she walked the rest of the way at \(5\) kilometers per hour.

In all, it took her \(44\) minutes to reach her friend’s house. In kilometers rounded to the nearest tenth, how far did Samia walk?
solution:
Samia bicycled and walked equal distances, so let each distance be \(d\) kilometers. Since time equals distance divided by speed, her bicycling and walking times were \(d/17\) and \(d/5\) hours.

The total time was \(44/60\) hours, giving
\[
\frac{d}{17}+\frac{d}{5}=\frac{44}{60}=\frac{11}{15}.
\]
Combining the fractions and solving,
\[
\frac{5d+17d}{85}=\frac{11}{15},
\qquad
d=\frac{11}{15}\cdot\frac{85}{22}=\frac{17}{6}=2.8333\ldots.
\]
Thus she walked \(\boxed{2.8\text{ kilometers}}\) to the nearest tenth, choice (C).
